title: Primary f of alpha I + AB reconstructed from f of alpha I + BA
expression_sketch:
Let A lie in C^{m x n} and B in C^{n x m}, with m >= n, and assume BA is nonsingular. Let f be defined on the spectrum of alpha I_m + AB, and if m = n let f also be defined at alpha. Then (Higham Theorem 1.35)
  f(alpha I_m + AB) = f(alpha) I_m + A (BA)^{-1} ( f(alpha I_n + BA) - f(alpha) I_n ) B.
The n = 1 special case recovers a rank-one update formula for f(alpha I + u v^*). The inverse special case f(t) = 1/t, alpha = 1, rearranges to (I + AB)^{-1} = I - A (I + BA)^{-1} B. When BA is singular the displayed inverse (BA)^{-1} is unavailable; Higham notes separately that AB then has a zero eigenvalue of geometric multiplicity at least m-n (m > n).
latent_structure: One FUNCTION_1 f, evaluated at the two related matrices alpha I + AB and alpha I + BA, is linked by the first Newton divided difference g(t) = f[alpha + t, alpha] = (f(alpha+t) - f(alpha))/t via the identity f(alpha I + AB) = f(alpha) I + A g(BA) B. Nonsingular BA keeps the nodes alpha and alpha+t distinct on spec(BA). Singular BA is the confluent/degenerate stratum where that quotient form is not the stated theorem.

function_domains.f: Defined on the spectrum of alpha I_m + AB, and if m = n also defined at alpha (Higham Theorem 1.35 hypothesis). No holomorphy is assumed: 'Theorem 1.35 does not require analyticity.'

nonzero_conditions.statement: BA is nonsingular (Higham Theorem 1.35: 'assume that BA is nonsingular'), so (BA)^{-1} exists and 0 is not an eigenvalue of BA.
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 1.35

analytic_domains.statement: f is defined on the spectrum of alpha I_m + AB; if m = n, f is also defined at alpha (Higham Theorem 1.35). Then f is automatically defined on the spectrum of alpha I_n + BA and at alpha (Higham, first sentence of the proof, citing Theorem 1.32).
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 1.35 and Theorem 1.32

analytic_domains.statement: No holomorphy, Cauchy-integral, or C^k hypothesis is imposed on f beyond being defined on the stated spectra (Higham: 'Theorem 1.35 does not require analyticity').
analytic_domains.label: DECLARED
analytic_domains.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, paragraph after (1.31)

branch_conventions: f(alpha I + AB) and f(alpha I + BA) are primary matrix functions in the sense of Higham Chapter 1 (defined on the spectrum).
If f is multivalued, the same branch is used at corresponding eigenvalues of alpha I + AB and alpha I + BA as granted by Theorem 1.32.

limit_domains.statement: The displayed formula uses (BA)^{-1}, so it is not claimed when BA is singular. That singular stratum is excluded by the hypothesis, not taken as a limit inside Theorem 1.35.
limit_domains.label: DECLARED
limit_domains.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 1.35

source_provenance: N. J. Higham, Functions of Matrices: Theory and Computation, SIAM, 2008, Theorem 1.35 and equation (1.31); discussion after (1.31). DOI 10.1137/1.9780898717778
N. J. Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorems 1.32 and 1.34 (AB/BA spectral relation used in the proof)

derived_conditions.statement: The proof introduces g(t) = f[alpha + t, alpha] = t^{-1}(f(alpha+t) - f(alpha)), so f(alpha+t) = f(alpha) + t g(t), and invokes Corollary 1.34 to replace g(AB) by transport through A, B (Higham, proof of Theorem 1.35).
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 1.35 proof and Corollary 1.34

derived_conditions.statement: If m > n then AB has a zero eigenvalue of geometric multiplicity at least m-n, because Bx = 0 implies ABx = 0 and B has nullity at least m-n (Higham, discussion of AB versus BA before Theorem 1.35).
derived_conditions.label: DERIVED
derived_conditions.source: Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, discussion preceding Theorem 1.35

public_source: N. J. Higham, Functions of Matrices, SIAM 2008, Theorem 1.35 and (1.31), DOI 10.1137/1.9780898717778. Proof uses Corollary 1.34 and the Newton quotient g(t) = f[alpha+t, alpha].
why_not_cse_lgg: The two evaluations f(alpha I_m + AB) and f(alpha I_n + BA) are different-sized matrices. CSE will not reconstruct the larger from the smaller via A (BA)^{-1} (f_small - f(alpha) I) B. LGG will not invent the Newton quotient g of f at {alpha, alpha+t} as the kernel that intertwines AB and BA, nor treat singular BA as a different stratum.
proposer_leak_risk: Hide divided difference, Newton quotient, Sherman--Morrison--Woodbury, primary matrix function. Catalog members are the two evaluations f(alpha I + AB), f(alpha I + BA) and the displayed reconstruction (1.31).
notes: Do not insert holomorphy or a closed contour integral of a general f; Higham states the theorem does not require analyticity. Do not insert self-adjointness. Do not run (BA)^{-1} when BA is singular, and do not claim the singular case as a limit identity without a separate confluence statement. This is not the general interpolating-polynomial definition of f(M).
